title: Timberwolves @ Warriors — Steal wrongly credited to Towns, re-assigned to Anthony Edwards next day (Jan 27-28, 2022)
incident_summary: Early in the first quarter of the Timberwolves-Warriors game of Jan 27, 2022, Anthony Edwards intercepted a Stephen Curry pass (Curry was being pressured by Karl-Anthony Towns near the sideline). The steal was initially credited to Towns. After bettors posted over-0.5-steals Edwards wagers and questioned the play on social media, the NBA corrected the box score the next day (Jan 28): the steal was taken from Towns and credited to Edwards. The game score/total was never in dispute — a non-scoring stat correction documenting the league's post-game pipeline.
scoring_play: Edwards interception of a Curry pass near the sideline with Towns pressuring — steal attribution, not a scoring play.
affected_player: Karl-Anthony Towns (MIN) — steal removed; Anthony Edwards (MIN) — steal added

originally_reported.value: Steal credited to Karl-Anthony Towns; Edwards 0 steals

corrected_value.value: Steal taken from Towns, credited to Anthony Edwards (over 0.5 steals cashes on corrected books)

final_official.basis: Corrected official box score (ESPN). Game final score was never disputed and is out of scope — not asserted here.

sources_disagreed: Game-night box score (Towns steal) vs. corrected box score (Edwards steal)
Sportsbook grading split: FanDuel honored the correction (paid overs; left unders as winners) while BetMGM/DraftKings-style day-of-box settlement would not move

cause.detail: Suspected real-time attribution error by the in-game stat crew on a shared defensive play (two defenders involved). Exact crew-level cause undocumented.

timeline.event: Timberwolves @ Warriors; Edwards' early-Q1 interception is credited to Towns in the game-night box score.
NBA issues the week's second correction: steal moved from Towns to Edwards. FanDuel honors the change for over-0.5-steals wagers.
